title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.
intro: This training programme equips firms to see themselves the way a supervisor does: how authorities assess business models, financials, governance and risk, rate and prioritise firms, run inspections and interviews, and act on what they find.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give senior leaders and control functions an inside view of risk-based supervision, taught by former supervisors using the same frameworks, evidence and judgements authorities apply to firms. Participants leave able to assess their own firm as a supervisor would, prepare for meetings and inspections with confidence, and respond to findings in a way that builds a constructive relationship.
sections.What It Covers: Risk-based supervision and impact and probability, supervisory intensity and the supervisory cycle, business model analysis, financial analysis, governance assessment, risk management and controls, data, returns and thematic reviews, supervisory meetings, inspections and interviews, risk ratings, panels and findings, and building a constructive relationship.
Intended Audience: Chief executives, senior managers and executive directors who meet the supervisor
Heads of compliance, risk, finance and internal audit and their teams who prepare the firm for supervision
Company secretaries, regulatory liaison and relationship managers who coordinate supervisory engagement
Learning Objectives: Explain how risk-based supervision works and how authorities decide how closely to supervise the firm
Assess the firm's business model and financial position using the analysis supervisors apply
Evaluate the firm's governance, risk management and controls against supervisory expectations and red flags
Prepare directors and managers for supervisory meetings, inspections and interviews
Interpret risk ratings and findings and respond with credible, evidence-based remediation
Design a strategy for a constructive, open and no-surprises relationship with the authority
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module pairs the supervisor's method with practical preparation for the firm, using case studies, exercises and mock supervisory meetings, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and supervisory category.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of senior management, compliance, risk or finance work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of working for an authority is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)

modules.title: Inside the Authority: Risk-Based Supervision
modules.summary: How authorities organise supervision around risk, combining the impact of a firm's failure with the probability of it happening, and why this framework shapes every interaction the firm has with its supervisor.
objectives: Explain the objectives and mandate that drive supervisory decisions
Explain how impact and probability combine into a view of the firm
Identify where the firm sits in its authority's framework and why
syllabus: Statutory objectives and outcomes-based supervision
Impact: size, customer reach, systemic importance and substitutability
Probability: inherent risk, controls, governance and financial resilience
International principles on risk-based supervision across sectors

modules.title: Supervisory Intensity and the Supervisory Cycle
modules.summary: How authorities set their own risk appetite, vary intensity across the regulated population and plan their work, and what each engagement model means in practice for the firm.
objectives: Explain how authorities allocate scarce supervisory resource
Distinguish the engagement models applied to high-impact and smaller firms
Anticipate the supervisory cycle and the touchpoints it creates
syllabus: The authority's risk appetite and tolerance for firm failure
Intensity tiers, firm categorisation and minimum engagement models
Supervisory plans, desk-based review and proactive versus reactive work
How firms move between categories and what triggers closer attention

modules.title: Your Business Model Through a Supervisor's Eyes
modules.summary: How supervisors analyse strategy and business models, test viability and sustainability, and spot a stretched model, so the firm can present and challenge its own plans in the same terms.
objectives: Characterise the firm's business model as a supervisor would
Assess viability and sustainability and the key dependencies
Recognise the signs of a stretched or failing business model
syllabus: Products, customers, channels, value chain and revenue drivers
Viability and sustainability: the supervisor's two questions
Dependencies: owners, outsourcers, distributors, banking partners and major clients
Signs of stress: rapid growth, outlier returns and concentration

modules.title: Your Financials Through a Supervisor's Eyes
modules.summary: How supervisors read financial statements, regulatory returns and projections, and how the firm can anticipate the questions its numbers will raise.
objectives: Read the firm's financial statements and returns with a supervisory lens
Assess capital, liquidity and the credibility of projections
Identify the financial red flags that prompt supervisory challenge
syllabus: Balance sheet, income statement, cash flow and related party disclosures
Capital, liquidity buffers, safeguarding and wind-down resources
Projections, assumptions and why strategies fail
Red flags: aggressive accounting, late filings and unexplained movements

modules.title: Governance as the Supervisor Assesses It
modules.summary: What supervisors look for when they assess governance, the evidence they use and the red flags that lower a rating, so the board and executives can test themselves first.
objectives: Explain the components of governance risk supervisors assess
Identify the evidence supervisors use, from board packs to minutes
Assess the firm's governance against common supervisory red flags
syllabus: Governance risk: board, management, accountability, culture and group influence
Evidence: board packs, minutes, evaluations and committee papers
Challenge versus confrontation, information asymmetry and dominant individuals
Rating governance and its link to other risk categories

modules.title: Risk Management and Controls: Working, Not Just Existing
modules.summary: How supervisors judge whether risk management and the control functions actually work, how they test controls, and how control quality changes the net risk rating.
objectives: Explain how supervisors move from inherent risk to net risk
Assess the stature, independence and resourcing of the control functions
Evidence that controls operate effectively, not merely on paper
syllabus: Risk appetite, risk identification and management information
Compliance, risk and internal audit: independence, stature and coverage
Walk-throughs, sample testing and outcomes evidence
Net risk: weighing controls against inherent risk

modules.title: Data, Returns and Thematic Reviews
modules.summary: How authorities use regulatory returns and data analytics to compare firms and find outliers, and how thematic reviews work, so the firm understands what its data says before the supervisor does.
objectives: Explain how supervisors use returns and data to identify outliers
Assure the accuracy and consistency of the firm's regulatory reporting
Prepare for and respond to thematic reviews and information requests
syllabus: Regulatory returns as supervisory data: ownership, accuracy and sign-off
Peer comparison, outlier analysis and supervisory dashboards
Thematic reviews: triggers, sampling, questionnaires and feedback
Information requests: scope, deadlines and consistency of answers

modules.title: Supervisory Meetings, Inspections and Interviews
modules.summary: How supervisors plan meetings, on-site inspections and interviews with directors and managers, what they test, and how the firm prepares people and documents without scripting them.
objectives: Explain how supervisors plan meetings, inspections and interviews
Prepare directors and managers to give accurate, owned answers
Manage document requests, logistics and follow-up during an inspection
syllabus: Visit planning, document requests and interview schedules
What supervisors test in interviews with chairs, executives and control functions
Preparation: briefing packs, consistency and owning the answer
Mock supervisory meeting with the chief executive and chair

modules.title: Risk Ratings, Panels, Findings and Remediation
modules.summary: How supervisory assessments are challenged and calibrated in internal panels, how ratings become findings letters and risk mitigation programmes, and how the firm responds credibly.
objectives: Explain how panels calibrate ratings and what drives the outcome
Interpret findings letters and the supervisory tools that may follow
Design a remediation response that fixes root causes and closes with evidence
syllabus: Risk governance panels: pack, challenge and calibration of ratings
Findings letters, risk mitigation programmes and deadlines
Escalation tools: attestations, skilled person reviews, directions and licence conditions
Responding to findings: accuracy, root causes and evidence of closure

modules.title: A Constructive Relationship and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around building trust with the authority, followed by a workshop in which participants assess a case-study firm as a supervisor would and plan its engagement.
objectives: Design an engagement strategy built on openness and no surprises
Apply the supervisor's method to assess a firm end to end
Produce an action plan to strengthen the firm's supervisory relationship
syllabus: Openness, notifications and the cost of surprises
Relationship mapping, regulatory liaison and board reporting on supervision
Common misunderstandings between firms and supervisors
Workshop: assessing a case-study firm and planning its supervisory engagement

related.title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
related.summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.

related.title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.

related.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.

related.title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation: From Risk Assessment to Closure
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors reach findings and how licensees can respond with remediation that fixes root causes and closes issues on evidence.
